name: Visited link (:visited) history sniffing
plain: Used to detect which links the person had visited by styling :visited links.
meaning: Browsers lie to getComputedStyle for :visited since 2010, but timing, scroll and rendering side channels remained. Chrome 136 partitions :visited links, ending cross-site history probing.

steps: Check style or timing for visited state

limits.headline: Can't find which links you visited by testing link colours anymore
limits.user_action: Nothing. Chrome 136 and other browsers already block it
can: Show visited links in a different colour that you can see
Try timing and scroll tricks, which now work far less in current browsers
cannot: See which sites you visited from link colours
Work across sites in Chrome 136 and later
Work in Firefox and Safari, which hide the answer
limits.differs: Chrome 136 now keeps visited links separate per site. Firefox and Safari blocked the main trick earlier.

story.what_it_is: Old trick: a site styled links so visited and unvisited ones looked different, then read which pages you had seen.

marketing.name: Privacy and the :visited selector
marketing.pitch: MDN explains how browsers limit what styles can apply to visited links, so sites cannot see your history.

story.for_you: Today you are mostly protected. Browsers tell pages that every link looks unvisited, so a page cannot learn which sites you saw. It is why visited links only change color on your own screen.
story.for_makers: In the past, ad and data sellers used it to learn which banks, shops or news sites a visitor had been to. Browsers fixed it around 2010 and later, so it now works as a security lesson more than a tool.

use_cases.example: Before the fix, a malicious page could list which bank sites you had visited by testing their links.
Older ad scripts checked which shopping sites you visited to target ads.
A store could check for competitor links in your history to adjust its price or coupon.
A social network could guess your interests from visited links to other sites.
A news site could see if you had read a rival's story, and tailor its message.
Browser makers lock down which styles can use visited links, so apps still show purple links but pages cannot read them.
A security course shows how the old attack worked to explain browser privacy design.

technical_bounds: Same-site history probing still possible if site is the history owner
Lie-based mitigation not perfect for rendering side channels

history.change: Partitioned :visited link history by top frame and link origin
